evidence: Receiving DO2 11.41 mg/L at 50.0 h then 1.90 mg/L at 50.2 h, persisting 1.60-1.96 mg/L through 52.0 h — below 2.0 mg/L minimum
No analogous collapse in source-1/2/3, which stay ~8-14 mg/L through 96 h
P assay 3.06 g/L at 48 h (delayed 4 h) — production active pre-collapse
Forward model: transfer multiplier 0.423, cost 3.46 estimated from change at ~50 h
Model comparison: strong_feed_reduction best (min DO 1.04, deficit 5.55, below-limit 9.2 h, mass 194.5 kg) vs combined (0.91/7.61/9.6/194.0) and increase_air (0.82/9.64/13/193.9)
submission.rationale: At 50.2 h the receiving batch's DO2 abruptly fell from ~11.4 to ~1.9 mg/L and remains below the 2.0 mg/L operating floor through the decision time (52.0 h), unlike any source batch. The source-calibrated forward model attributes this to a severe drop in oxygen-transfer capacity (~42% of nominal), so the highest-magnitude bounded intervention is warranted. Among allowed actions, strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6, air x1.15) minimizes predicted time below the oxygen limit and oxygen deficit while retaining essentially full product mass (predicted ~194.5 kg, the highest of all interventions, since growth continues under restored-but-partial oxygen supply). A stop would count zero production; KEEP or air-only would prolong oxygen-limit violation. The model flags even this action as marginally infeasible under nominal parameters, so this is the best available bounded choice pending review; an extra product assay was not requested because product concentration is not the binding issue — oxygen constraint compliance is, and waiting (KEEP) during assay turnaround would extend the violation.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal, source-calibrated, and not the hidden receiving realization; all sensitivity members show minimum DO below 2.0 mg/L, so the intervention may not fully restore constraint compliance — a follow-up aeration repair/review beyond the bounded action set may be needed. P assays lag 4 h, so the true current product state is uncertain; product mass could differ. Sensor noise (~±0.3 mg/L) is small relative to the collapse magnitude, so the anomaly itself is high-confidence.

evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 50.0h = 11.41 mg/L, then 50.2-52.0h readings 1.60-2.17 mg/L, below minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0
Latest delayed assay (sampled 48.0h, available 52.0h): P = 3.06 g/L, production is active and must be retained
Allowed actions: keep [1.0,1.0], reduce_feed [0.8,1.0], increase_air [1.0,1.15], combined [0.8,1.15], strong_feed_reduction [0.6,1.15], stop null
Source batches show normal DO2 decline (~8-9 mg/L) during high production with no crash, indicating the receiving crash is a receiving-specific oxygen supply problem
submission.rationale: The receiving fermenter shows a sharp oxygen collapse: DO2 fell from ~11.4 mg/L at 50.0h to ~1.9 mg/L at 50.2h and stayed at 1.6-2.0 mg/L through 52.0h, violating the 2.0 mg/L minimum oxygen constraint. Source batches under identical elapsed profiles maintained DO2 of ~10-11 mg/L at this age, so this is a receiving-process-specific aeration shortfall, not normal metabolic drawdown. The bounded action that directly addresses oxygen supply without sacrificing product mass is increase_air ([1.0, 1.15] feed/air factors): it restores DO2 headroom while keeping the feed rate unchanged, preserving ongoing production (P was 3.06 g/L at 48h and rising). reduce_feed/combined/strong_feed_reduction would all cut substrate delivery and hence counted product mass, and stop yields zero production. keep is rejected because the DO2 constraint is already violated and oxygen availability is the demonstrated bottleneck.
submission.uncertainty: Magnitude of the aeration deficit is unknown; a 15% air increase may only partially restore DO2 given the abrupt step-like drop (possible equipment fault). Product kinetics under reduced DO2 are also uncertain, so the 48h assay value may not reflect current trajectory. If DO2 does not recover after increased air, a follow-up combined action may be needed, but this action is bounded and retains full feed/product mass.
